He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]]. ==Early life== Green was born in [[Sydney]] to Australian mother Cahla and American-born father Delmas. His parents met while both were playing semi-professional basketball in Australia.{{cite web |url=http://www.espn.com/espn/story/_/id/25794761/arizona-recruit-josh-green-australian-first-basketball-player-cbb |title=Josh Green is an Australian first, basketball player second |publisher=ESPN |date=21 January 2019}} The couple decided to raise a family in the north-west Sydney suburb of [[Castle Hill, New South Wales|Castle Hill]] where Josh began playing basketball at the age of five when his mother started coaching him. Along with playing local basketball for the Hills Hornets as a child, Green tried an array of sports as a junior and excelled in [[Australian rules football]], [[Sport of athletics|athletics]], basketball, [[Rugby football|rugby]], [[association football|soccer]] and [[swimming (sport)|swimming]]. By the age of 10, he had been selected to represent his home state of [[New South Wales]] in nine separate sports.{{cite web |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2798917-preps-hoops-star-josh-green-is-ready-to-take-his-next-step |title=Preps star Josh Green ready to commit |publisher=Bleacher Report |date=5 October 2018}} In fifth grade, Green traveled more than 12 hours by car to the [[Outback|outback]] town of [[Broken Hill, New South Wales|Broken Hill]] in an attempt to gain selection for the under-12 state basketball team and was told he was good enough to be on the team but would have to wait a year or two so the older boys could play. 12 months later, he captained the under-12 NSW Metro state team to a national title. Green switched to play club basketball for Penrith in 2013 and the decision paid off when he was selection to represent the under-14 and under-16 New South Wales state teams in successive years as a bottom-ager.{{cite web |url=https://westernweekender.com.au/2020/04/josh-green-on-verge-of-nba-dream-becoming-reality/ |title=Josh Green on verge of NBA dream becoming reality |publisher=The Western Weekender |date=16 April 2020}} Green was also a prodigious [[Australian rules football]]er in his younger years{{cite web |url=https://www.news.com.au/sport/basketball/ben-simmons-has-already-taken-high-school-basketball-star-josh-green-under-his-wing/news-story/3aff201301a79818709136f25b1a68e2 |title=Ben Simmons has already taken high school basketball star Josh Green under his wing |publisher=News.com.au |date=31 January 2019}}{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R6MTeMvbwDE |title=Arizona Wildcats' Josh Green - Australia's Next Basketball Star |publisher=Trans World Sport |date=26 February 2018}}{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=llxPus2AtwU |title=Josh Green Nike Hoop Summit Interview |publisher=Draft Express |date=18 April 2018}} while playing locally for the Westbrook Bulldogs and would regularly attend [[Sydney Swans]] home games with his father. Green claims to have "loved" playing Australian football{{cite web |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/a-weekend-with-josh-green-australias-next-sporting-superstar/news-story/6b2edff6900af7f17dab4c28420e02b8 |title=A weekend with Josh Green, Australia’s next sporting superstar |publisher=Fox Sports Australia |date=8 March 2019}}{{cite web |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/josh-green-pumped-to-represent-australia-on-the-hardwood-in/article_cd1c4d05-f236-5555-9c89-62221caf7ba6.html |title=Josh Green pumped to represent Australia on the hardwood in Hoop Summit game |publisher=Arizona Daily Star |date=11 April 2019}}{{cite web |url=http://www.espn.com.au/espn/story/_/id/26801651/australia-newest-basketball-star-cbb |title=Josh Green: Australia's latest basketball star headed for Arizona |publisher=ESPN Australia |date=24 May 2019}} and has "always been a big Swans fan", naming [[Adam Goodes]] and [[Lance Franklin]] as his favourite players growing up.{{cite web |url=https://wwos.nine.com.au/basketball/basketball-josh-green-reacts-to-comparisons-to-australian-nba-star-ben-simmons/b3b17277-225f-42d5-950d-f9885d29e997 |title=Rising Australian basketball star and 'freak athlete' Josh Green on track for bright NBA future |publisher=Wide World of Sports |date=8 February 2019}} Such was his talent in Australian football, the Swans and fellow professional franchise [[Greater Western Sydney Football Club|Greater Western Sydney Giants]] offered him a place in their junior developmental academies. At the age of 13, Green accepted an offer to join the Giants' academy.{{cite web |url=https://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/sport/basketball/josh-green-becomes-first-australian-since-ben-simmons-to-be-mcdonalds-allamerican/news-story/9755d636f4a00bbc40c7e86847b5df3a |title=Josh Green becomes first Australian since Ben Simmons to be McDonald’s All-American |publisher=Daily Telegraph |date=25 January 2019}}{{subscription relocated to [[Phoenix, Arizona]]{{cite web |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2015/12/28/green-brothers-lift-mountain-ridge-title-hopes/77982208/ |title=Green brothers lift |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SGpvDZNcAL8 |title=5 Star Arizona Commit Josh Green Q+A |publisher=BallerVisions |date=23 December 2018}} ==High school career== While in Australia, Green attended [[The King's School, Parramatta|The King's School]] in Sydney and dominated the local basketball scene so much that he was selected to represent the New South Wales' under 16 state team at the age of 13.{{cite web |url=https://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/newslocal/west/sport/four-youngsters-from-penrith-basketball-selected-into-nsw-under16-state-teams/news-story/8586d588e9c585c53171b18c3e568e00 |title=Four youngsters from Penrith Basketball selected into NSW under-16 State teams |publisher=Daily Telegraph |date=29 May 2014}}{{cite web the Australian taking over the American high school basketball scene |publisher=Fox Sports Australia |date=29 September 2017}} Later that year, the Green family relocated to [[Phoenix, Arizona]], and in 2015, Josh enrolled at [[Mountain Ridge High School (Arizona)|Mountain Ridge High School]], where he impressed.[https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2015/12/28/green-brothers-lift-mountain-ridge-title-hopes/77982208/ Green brothers lift Mountain Ridge with title hopes] In 2017, he transferred to the [[IMG Academy]] in Florida[https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/meet-josh-green-the-australian-taking-over-the-american-high-school-basketball-scene/news-story/e168bdba13cbb0ff848dccb3bf045179 Meet Josh Green, the Australian taking over the American high school basketball scene] and became a five-star draft prospect.{{cite web |url=http://www.couriermail.com.au/sport/more-sports/josh-green-has-been-rated-a-fivestar-recruit-as-us-colleges-continue-to-fight-for-him/news-story/ee70c4f89019efd72c05374077949a41 |title=Josh Green has been rated a five-star recruit, as US colleges continue to fight for him |publisher=Courier Mail |date=11 January 2018}} In the final game of his high school career, Green led IMG to a national championship victory with a 65–55 win over [[La Lumiere School|La Lumiere]] and was subsequently named MVP of the championship game.{{cite web |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nba/australias-josh-green-leads-img-academy-to-geico-nationals-championship/news-story/074bbabbff7706f4101a9ae041eee254 |title=Australia’s Josh Green leads IMG Academy to GEICO Nationals Championship |publisher=Fox Sports Australia |date=7 April 2019}} He was selected for the [[2019 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]], along with fellow UA recruit [[Nico Mannion]].{{cite web |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/pascoe/arizona-wildcats-signees-nico-mannion-josh-green-named-to-mcdonald/article_9e582720-2016-11e9-9e1b-d32d50376ff2.html |title=Arizona Wildcats signees Nico Mannion, Josh Green named to McDonald's All-American Game |publisher=Arizona Daily Star |date=24 January 2019}} ===Recruiting=== Green received an offer to join the [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova Wildcats]] in April 2018.{{cite web |url=https://www.vuhoops.com/2018/4/23/17273898/villanova-basketball-recruiting-josh-green-offer |title=Villanova offers 2019 guard Josh Green |publisher=VU Hoops |date=23 April 2018}} In July 2018, he received an offer to join the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]].{{cite web |url=https://247sports.com/college/north-carolina/Article/Josh-Green-Tar-Heels-Offer-Basketball-Scholarship-119856525/ |title=Tar Heels Offer Scholarship to Josh Green |publisher=247 Sports - North Carolina |date=31 July 2018}} Green was considered a top player in the 2019 recruiting class by [[247Sports.com|247Sports]], [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] and [[ESPN]]. On October 4, 2018, Green committed to play for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]] over [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]], [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]], [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]] and [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV]]. Green is a consensus five-star prospect out of [[IMG Academy]] in [[Bradenton, Florida]]. In October 2018, Green signed his NLI to the University of Arizona for basketball.{{cite web |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/college/ua/2018/10/04/arizona-wildcats-basketball-5-star-guard-josh-green-commits/1524889002/ |title=Josh Green joins Nico Mannion in committing to Arizona |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/pascoe/on-sean-miller-s-conversations-with-officials-at-ucla-josh/article_ccff0fe8-5b8f-11ea-84c5-e32b03bfe40c.html |accessdate=March 1, 2020 |work=[[Arizona Daily Star]] |date=March 1, 2020}} Green averaged 12.0 points, 4.6 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 1.5 steals per game for the Wildcats as a freshman while shooting 36.1% from three-point range. Following the season, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Josh Green entering draft after freshman year at Arizona |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29021904/josh-green-entering-draft-freshman-year-arizona |accessdate=April 10, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=April 10, 2020}} ==National team career== Green was named in the 24-man squad selected to represent the [[Australia men's national basketball team|Australian national team]] in [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Asia)|FIBA World Cup Qualifiers]] against [[Qatar national basketball team|Qatar]] and [[Kazakhstan national basketball team|Kazakhstan]] in September 2018.{{cite web |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/josh-green-talks-aussie-boomers-squad-nod-looking-up-to-ben-simmons-and-dant-exum-and-getting-an-offer-from-north-carolina/news-story/f16404f8c221cd86d7075051f92592c1 |title=Josh Green talks Aussie Boomers squad nod, looking up to Ben Simmons and Dante Exum, and getting an offer from North Carolina |publisher=Fox Sports Australia |date=3 August 2018}} However, a torn labrum in his right shoulder prevented him from making his international debut. In January 2019, Green revealed his ambitions to represent Australia at the [[2020 Summer Olympics|2020 Tokyo Olympics]]. On February 6, 2019, Green was named in the 23-man squad selected to represent [[Australia national under-19 basketball team|Australia's Under-19 national team]] at the [[2019 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]].{{cite web |url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/potential-nba-draftee-josh-green-named-in-emus-squad-20190206-p50w2s.html |title=Potential NBA draftee Josh Green named in Emus squad |publisher=Sydney Morning Herald |date=6 February 2019}} In March 2019, Green signalled his aspiration to represent Australia at the [[2019 FIBA World Cup]].{{cite web |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/exclusive-josh-green-wants-to-make-his-australian-boomers-debut-in-the-2019-fiba-world-cup/news-story/e06b157ce8cec14bdbc9f29275200a77 |title=Exclusive: Josh Green wants to make his Australian Boomers debut in the 2019 FIBA World Cup |publisher=Fox Sports Australia |date=9 March 2019}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]] | 30 || 30 || 30.9 || .424 || .361 || .780 || 4.6 || 2.6 || 1.5 || .4 || 12.0 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Josh is the son of Cahla and Delmas Green. He has three siblings: Jay, Ky, and Maya. His father played at Oregon Tech, while both of his parents played professionally in Australia. Josh’s brother Jay currently plays for the [[Northern Arizona Lumberjacks men's basketball|Northern Arizona Lumberjacks]].{{cite news |last1=Hartzler |first1=Lance |title=NAU men's basketball adds second graduate transfer, signs UNLV guard Jay Green |url=https://azdailysun.com/sports/local/nau-mens-basketball-adds-second-graduate-transfer-signs-unlv-guard-jay-green/article_b1f3ed6c-6928-5e4d-bb87-704334f695b2.html |accessdate=November 6, 2020 |work=[[Arizona Daily Sun]] |date=April 20, 2020}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://arizonawildcats.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/josh-green/10609 Arizona Wildcats bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Green, Josh}} [[Category:2000 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Arizona Wildcats men's basketball players]] [[Category:Australian expatriate basketball people in the United States]] [[Category:Australian men's basketball players]] [[Category:Australian people of African-American descent]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Sydney]] [[Category:Basketball players from New South Wales]]
